description: The five recordings evaluated in the paper, as published on TUdatalib (DOI 10.48328/tudatalib-2246). Paths are relative to the dataset root (the folder that contains data/). Channels map the three muscle sites to the CSV columns; the wiring differs between sessions. Trims are applied after resampling to 330 Hz. step_onset_s is the measured start of the first speed step (4.0 km/h) in the trimmed time base: each raw ramp holds exactly six speed steps between a standstill before and after, and the program starts with the walking onset, so the trims cut into the first step. The holdout keys define the two windows per training ramp that were removed from network training; they lie on the nominal protocol grid (step i at i * speed_duration_s after the trim) and therefore do not coincide with the measured speed steps.

Ramp_60s.label: S1 speed ramp, 60 s per step

Ramp_60s_v2.label: S2 speed ramp, 60 s per step

Ramp_30s.label: S2 speed ramp, 30 s per step

notes.drop_first_sample: The paper's evaluation read the session-2 source files with a loader that skipped their first line as a header, although these files have none. The published CSVs keep that first sample. Setting drop_first_sample reproduces the paper's input exactly; scripts/reproduce.py --keep-first-sample runs on the complete files instead.
notes.Step_6.7_4.6: Named after the step-change protocol; the analysis window contains only the first speed (6.57 km/h), so the paper calls it the 6.7 km/h recording and treats it as constant speed.
notes.RF saturation: The S1 Rectus Femoris readout (ferro_1) is saturated for the whole S1 ramp and for most of the 6.7 km/h recording. The multi-sensor configurations use it as recorded, as in the paper.
